title: How immunosuppressant drugs block T cell activation and growth
ariaLabel: Schematic of T cell activation: antigen signalling through calcineurin switches on interleukin-2, lymphocytes need purine synthesis to divide, interleukin-2 signalling through mTOR drives growth, and inflammatory genes are switched on by transcription factors. Tacrolimus and ciclosporin block calcineurin, mycophenolate and azathioprine block purine synthesis, sirolimus blocks mTOR, and glucocorticoids reduce inflammatory gene expression.
caption: Schematic, not to scale. Flow and levels are qualitative and illustrative; no dose, concentration or lipid value is shown or implied.

edges.label: calcineurin
edges.info: Tacrolimus and ciclosporin bind immunophilins and block calcineurin, so NFAT is not activated and interleukin-2 is not made.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: purine synthesis
edges.info: Mycophenolate (IMPDH) and azathioprine (as thiopurines) block purine synthesis. Lymphocytes depend heavily on it, so they divide less.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: mTOR
edges.info: Sirolimus and everolimus block mTOR, so T cells do not respond to interleukin-2 by growing.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: gene transcription
edges.info: Glucocorticoids act through their receptor to lower transcription of many inflammatory genes (for example through NF-kB).
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

sources: Where each class acts. Calcineurin inhibitors block interleukin-2 production, mycophenolate and azathioprine block purine synthesis, mTOR inhibitors block growth signalling, and glucocorticoids reduce inflammatory gene transcription. This is standard teaching in the pharmacology texts the PrepNucleus lessons cite (Katzung; KD Tripathi) and were not checked against a linked source here, so they are flagged for review.
simplified: Antibodies and biologics, methotrexate, cyclophosphamide, belatacept, infection and cancer risks, drug levels and monitoring, interactions (notably cytochrome P450), and which drug suits which condition are left out. T cell activation is drawn as a teaching score. Levels and the size of each effect are illustrative. The drug choices are teaching toggles of a class: no named drug, dose or schedule is shown or implied, and the figure does not say who should or should not take any of them.
